package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: companies
  from: response
  value: "return response.data || []"

- emit: totalResults
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || []).length"

- emit: limit
  from: response
  value: "return Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.round(config.limit || 25)), 100)"

- emit: offset
  from: response
  value: "return Math.max(0, Math.round(config.offset || 0))"
files.api/run.yaml:
# The one Hunter endpoint that takes the key in a HEADER rather than the query, and the one
# that POSTs. Both are the vendor's choice, not an inconsistency here.
#
# `query` REPLACES the filters when set, which is Hunter's rule: sending both makes the
# filters silently win and the query do nothing. The body is an expression so that whole
# branch can be expressed, and so an empty filter is left out rather than sent.
#
# Note the shapes: industry, technology, keywords and companyType want { include: [...] },
# headcount wants a bare array, and country wants a list of { country } objects. That is
# Hunter's API, transcribed rather than tidied.

- name: discover
  method: POST
  url: https://api.hunter.io/v2/discover
  credential: { $ref: hunter#headerCredential }
  body: >-
    return Object.assign(
      {
        limit: Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.round(config.limit || 25)), 100),
        offset: Math.max(0, Math.round(config.offset || 0))
      },
      String(config.query || '').trim()
        ? { query: String(config.query).trim() }
        : Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
            industry: String(config.industry || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
            technology: String(config.technology || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
            keywords: String(config.keywords || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
            company_type: String(config.companyType || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
          }).filter(e => e[1].length > 0).map(e => [e[0], { include: e[1] }])
          .concat(
            String(config.headcount || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean).length
              ? [['headcount', String(config.headcount).split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)]]
              : [],
            String(config.country || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean).length
              ? [['headquarters_location', { include: String(config.country).split(',')
                  .map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean).map(c => ({ country: c.toUpperCase() })) }]]
              : [],
            String(config.similarTo || '').trim()
              ? [['similar_to', String(config.similarTo).trim()]]
              : []
          ))
    )
  transport: json
  error: { $ref: hunter#error }
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    query:
      type: string
      title: Query
      description: >-
        A natural-language description of the companies you want. When set it REPLACES every
        filter below, which is Hunter's own rule rather than ours.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    industry:
      type: string
      title: Industry
      description: Comma-separated industries
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    country:
      type: string
      title: Country
      description: Comma-separated two-letter country codes, e.g. 'GB, US'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    headcount:
      type: string
      title: Headcount
      description: Comma-separated size bands, e.g. '1-10, 11-50'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    technology:
      type: string
      title: Technology
      description: Comma-separated technologies the company uses
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    keywords:
      type: string
      title: Keywords
      description: Comma-separated keywords to match
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    companyType:
      type: string
      title: Company Type
      description: Comma-separated types, e.g. 'privately held, public company'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    similarTo:
      type: string
      title: Similar To
      description: A domain to find lookalikes of
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    limit:
      type: number
      title: Limit
      default: 25
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
    offset:
      type: number
      title: Offset
      default: 0
      minimum: 0
"ui:order":
  [query, industry, country, headcount, technology, keywords, companyType, similarTo, limit, offset]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Filters may template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: companies
    type: array
    description: Matched companies with domain, organisation and email counts
  - name: totalResults
    type: number
    description: How many companies came back
  - name: limit
    type: number
    description: Page size used
  - name: offset
    type: number
    description: Offset used

credentials:
  - name: hunterCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Hunter.io
files.node.yaml:
type: HunterDiscover
kind: PromiseNode
name: Hunter Discover
category: Go To Market
color: "#FF5500"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1781366295/gravity/icons/hunter.png
description: Build a target-company list from criteria or a natural-language query
whenToUse: >
  Pick to BUILD a target-company list from criteria (industry, tech stack, size, location)
  or a natural-language query, the starting point for prospecting, with tech-stack and
  lookalike filters. Use it to discover unknown companies by criteria; if you already have a
  domain you do not need a discovery step.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Apollo too, for its other four nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.hunter.io]
files.test.yaml:
testData:
  config:
    query: B2B SaaS companies in London
    industry: ""
    country: ""
    headcount: ""
    technology: ""
    keywords: ""
    companyType: ""
    similarTo: ""
    limit: 5
    offset: 0
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    companies: "return Array.isArray(output.companies)"
    limit: "return output.limit === 5"
